name: Hilbert's Sixteenth Problem: Limit Cycles in Planar Systems

children.name: Quintic Liénard Systems Bound
System Definition
Scalar Equation: x'' + F'(x)x' + x = 0
Primitive F: Polynomial of degree deg(F) <= 5
No Restrictions: Signs, parity, hyperbolicity, or amplitude
Main Theorem Results
Maximum Limit Cycles: Exactly two in R^2
Sharpness: Attained by degree-five polynomials
Conjecture Proved: Solves Lins Neto–de Melo–Pugh for deg = 5
Methodology & Proof Steps
Arc Coordinates: Parametrized half-orbits by peak height and width r
Quadratic Fitting: Global interpolation using quadratic profiles
Model Inequality: Schwarzian identity and Riccati linearization
Shape Comparisons: Curvature and slope-intercept monotonicity
Sign Partition: Counting isolated zeros of matching function ∆(r)
Uniform Boundedness for Degree d
Main Theorem: Limit cycles bounded by finite constant B(d)
Scope: Bounded globally in planar fields of maximum degree d
Core Proof Strategy
Logarithmic Flags: Record ordered large scales and logarithmic ties
Separation Theorem: Asymptotic expansion tree on nested complex domains
Packet Calculus: Differentiated implicit and ordinary chart closure
Matching Equations: Representation of returns across local passages
Absolute Isolated-Zero Criterion: Dimensional reduction and elimination
Passage Models & Analytic Tools
One-Rate Passages: Regular and stable transfers with one large clock
Two-Scale Passages: Comparable or widely separated logarithmic scales
Additive Passages: Damped transverse states and residual passage models
Subanalytic Preparation: Subdivision into finite pole-free boxes and annuli
